nodes.summary: Planar arcs are parametrized by the closed unit interval $[0, 1]$ of real numbers.
nodes.title: Parameter interval of unit arcs

nodes.summary: For every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $c \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $|e^{i\theta}\gamma(t) + c| \le 1$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$; that is, the closed disk of radius $1$ centred at $0$ covers every unit arc.
nodes.title: The closed unit disk covers every unit arc

nodes.summary: The closed disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$ is a convex universal cover: it is nonempty, convex, and covers every unit arc.
nodes.title: The closed unit disk is a convex universal cover

nodes.summary: The convex cover area infimum, the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the Lebesgue areas of all convex universal covers in $\mathbb{C}$, is not $\infty$.
nodes.title: The infimal area of convex universal covers is finite

nodes.summary: The convex cover area infimum is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the set of convex cover areas, that is, the infimum of the Lebesgue areas of all convex universal covers $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Infimal area of convex universal covers

nodes.summary: The set of convex cover areas, the Lebesgue areas of all convex universal covers in $\mathbb{C}$, is nonempty; that is, some convex universal cover exists.
nodes.title: The set of convex cover areas is nonempty

nodes.summary: The set of convex cover areas is the set of all values $\operatorname{vol}(\Omega) \in [0, \infty]$, where $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ ranges over the convex universal covers and $\operatorname{vol}$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Areas of convex universal covers

nodes.summary: The convex worm cover constant is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The convex worm cover constant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The convex worm cover constant is the real number obtained from the convex cover area infimum, the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the Lebesgue areas of all convex universal covers in $\mathbb{C}$, by the conversion $[0, \infty] \to \mathbb{R}$ that is the identity on finite values and sends $\infty$ to $0$.
nodes.title: Moser's convex worm cover constant

nodes.summary: The cover area infimum, the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the Lebesgue areas of all universal covers in $\mathbb{C}$ (nonempty sets that cover every unit arc, not necessarily convex), is not $\infty$.
nodes.title: The infimal area of universal covers is finite

nodes.summary: The infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of the areas $\lambda(\Omega)$ of the universal covers $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$, applied as an outer measure since $\Omega$ need not be measurable.
nodes.title: Infimal area of a universal cover

nodes.summary: The set of values $\lambda(\Omega) \in [0, \infty]$, where $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ ranges over the universal covers and $\lambda$ is Lebesgue outer measure on $\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$, is nonempty.
nodes.title: The set of universal cover areas is nonempty

nodes.summary: The set of values $\lambda(\Omega) \in [0, \infty]$, where $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ ranges over the universal covers and $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$, applied as an outer measure since $\Omega$ need not be measurable.
nodes.title: Areas of universal covers

nodes.summary: A set $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ covers every unit arc when for every unit arc $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$, that is, every continuous map whose total variation (length) is exactly $1$, there are an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $\tau \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $e^{i\theta} \gamma(t) + \tau \in \Omega$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: Sets that cover every unit arc

nodes.summary: The empty set $\emptyset \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ does not cover every unit arc: not every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ can be mapped into $\emptyset$ by a rotation followed by a translation.
nodes.title: The empty set does not cover every unit arc

nodes.summary: For every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $c \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $|e^{i\theta}\gamma(t) + c| \le 1/2$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The disk of diameter one covers every unit arc

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that the closed disk $D = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1/2\}$ covers every unit arc: for every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $c \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $e^{i\theta}\gamma(t) + c \in D$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The disk of diameter one covers every unit arc (claim)

nodes.summary: The closed disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1/2\}$ of radius $1/2$ centred at $0$.
nodes.title: Disk of radius one half

nodes.summary: Let $H = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1/2,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 0\}$. For every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $c \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $e^{i\theta}\gamma(t) + c \in H$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The half-disk of diameter one covers every unit arc

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that the closed half-disk $H = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1/2,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 0\}$ covers every unit arc: for every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $c \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $e^{i\theta}\gamma(t) + c \in H$ for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The half-disk of diameter one covers every unit arc (claim)

nodes.summary: The closed upper half-disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1/2,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 0\}$ of radius $1/2$ centred at $0$.
nodes.title: Semidisk of radius one half

nodes.summary: A set $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a convex universal cover when it is nonempty, convex (as a subset of the real plane $\mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$), and covers every unit arc: for every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\tau \in \mathbb{C}$ with $e^{i\theta} \gamma(t) + \tau \in \Omega$ for all $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: Convex universal covers

nodes.summary: Every convex universal cover $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a universal cover.
nodes.title: Convex universal covers are universal covers

nodes.summary: A set $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is a universal cover when it is nonempty and covers every unit arc: for every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ there are $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\tau \in \mathbb{C}$ with $e^{i\theta} \gamma(t) + \tau \in \Omega$ for all $t \in [0, 1]$. Neither convexity nor measurability of $\Omega$ is required.
nodes.title: Universal covers

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be the convex worm cover constant, the infimum of the areas of the nonempty convex sets $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ such that every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ can be moved into $\Omega$ by a rotation followed by a translation. Then $0.232239 \le \mu$.
nodes.title: Khandhawit–Pagonakis–Sriswasdi 2013 lower bound on the convex worm cover constant

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that $0.232239 \le \mu$, where $\mu$ is the convex worm cover constant: the infimum of the areas of the nonempty convex sets $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ such that every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ can be moved into $\Omega$ by a rotation followed by a translation.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be the convex worm cover constant, the infimum of the areas of the nonempty convex sets $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ such that every continuous curve $\gamma : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{C}$ of length exactly $1$ can be moved into $\Omega$ by a rotation followed by a translation. nodes.summary: For every real angle $\theta$ and every complex number $\tau$, the map $z \mapsto e^{i\theta} z + \tau$ of the complex plane is an isometry: it preserves the distance $|z - w|$ between any two points $z, w \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Direct rigid motions of the plane are isometries

nodes.summary: For a real angle $\theta$ and a complex number $\tau$, the motion with angle $\theta$ and translation $\tau$ sends $z \in \mathbb{C}$ to $e^{i\theta} z + \tau$: a rotation about the origin by $\theta$ followed by translation by $\tau$, with neither reflection nor rescaling.
nodes.title: Direct rigid motion of the plane

nodes.summary: The straight unit arc is the unit arc whose curve is the straight path $t \mapsto t$ from $[0, 1]$ to the complex plane, which traces the segment from $0$ to $1$ and has length $1$.
nodes.title: Straight unit arc

nodes.summary: A unit arc is a continuous map $\gamma$ from the closed interval $[0, 1]$ to the complex plane whose length, the total variation of $\gamma$ on $[0, 1]$, equals $1$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
